messages:
laura: quick follow-up from the postmortem — observed TTL drift in our token KV after last cluster migration. some tokens expired much sooner than expected, others lived far longer. we need clear owners for remediation, a short mitigation for prod, and an audit query to find affected users. tagging folks who volunteered in retro.

mike: ack. can you paste the postmortem link? also we should consider a temporary strict-validation toggle on the auth proxy so stale tokens are rejected even if KV shows them as valid. low-risk and reversible. :+1:

laura: postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4821 (notes attached). root cause summary: during Redis cluster migration a TTL write path used milliseconds in some binaries and seconds in others — inconsistent units. result = TTLs off by ~1000x in a subset of writes.

anita: i can own the fix in runtime — i'll normalize TTL writes to seconds and add a validation layer that refuses TTL if > 30d or < 10s. i'll open PR today and aim to ship canary by EOD Fri (assigning to me). @mike please review the canary policy. :memo:

samir: i'll add monitoring and an ad-hoc audit query. plan: 1) run audit to list token IDs with TTL > expected_range or TTL == 0; 2) alert on moving average of TTL values diverging more than 3x from baseline; 3) add an expvar metric for `token_ttl_unit` so we can detect ms vs s writes. example redis TTL check: 
```
# check ttl in seconds for keys with prefix
redis-cli --scan --pattern token:* | xargs -n1 -I{} redis-cli ttl {}
```
I'll post the query and perf implications in the ticket.

mike: good. add a CI unit test that asserts TTLs are written in seconds; catch the unit mismatch in premerge. can we also add an integration test that simulates migration? pinging @anita for test hooks.

laura: created follow-up JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4920 — summary: normalize token TTL writes + audit + runbook updates. action items below (short):
- ANITA: PR to normalize TTL + add runtime validation (due: 2026-04-03)
- SAMIR: audit query + alerting + metric (due: 2026-03-30)
- MIKE: CI test + canary policy review (due: 2026-03-31)
- OPS-ONCALL: runbook update + weekly check-ins x6 (start: 2026-03-25)

ops-oncall: scheduling weekly 30m check-ins on calendar starting 2026-03-25 — will invite owners. also adding a short playbook step: if audit finds >1000 affected tokens, run coordinated rotate with grace window.

anita: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3587 — includes TTL normalization and a toggle `AUTH_TTL_STRICT=true` behind feature flags. canary config added. linking to SEC-4920.

samir: posted the initial audit results in the ticket — ~2.4k tokens had TTL > expected_range, ~120 had TTL==0. I'll triage by service owner and create a CSV for targeted rotates. added the metric to staging.

mike: reviewed the PR, left minor comments. CI test added in branch `ci/ttl-check`. canary scheduled to 10% traffic for 2h then ramp.

laura: putting this here to make sure we don't lose momentum: please update the JIRA when each item moves to in-progress/done. will do a 1-week post-deploy check (2026-04-10) and capture any regression signals.

sre-bot: incident SEC-4821 status changed → "completed follow-ups in progress" (automated).

laura: final ask — add one-line note to runbook about unit conventions for TTLs and include the redis check snippet above. mark done here when updated. thanks all. :eyes:
